section_summary: This section (pages 1–80) consists primarily of diplomatic correspondence from March to June 1941 between the Japanese Embassy in Washington, the Department of State, and the Treasury Department regarding federal income tax exemptions under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code and sailing permits for Japanese officials, military officers, and scholars stationed in or departing from the United States. Prominent Japanese personnel documented include naval and military inspectors in New York, officials of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau and Financial Commission, and academic researchers such as Professor Toshinosuke Muto, who was sent to conduct atomic research. The records also encompass administrative memoranda and cross-reference sheets concerning foreign official status notifications under the Alien Registration Act of 1940, travel permits, customs bond refunds, and the organizational transfer of the Raw Silk Bureau in New York.

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests federal income tax exemption for Professor Toshinosuke Muto of Kyushu Imperial University while residing in the United States for atomic research.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy informs the Secretary of State that Professor Toshinosuke Muto was sent to the United States by the Japanese Government to conduct atomic research. His income is derived solely from the Japanese Government, and his residence in New York is at 640 Riverside Drive. The Ambassador requests that Muto be granted exemption from income taxes and that his name be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities. Page 2 is a duplicate copy of the note.
subfiles.title: Note No. 56 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Requesting Tax Exemption for Toshinosuke Muto

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Professor Toshinosuke Muto.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to the Secretary of the Treasury a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 56 concerning Professor Toshinosuke Muto of Kyushu Imperial University. In accordance with Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies that Japan grants an equivalent exemption to employees of the United States Government and that Muto's atomic research services are similar in character to services performed by U.S. employees abroad.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Toshinosuke Muto

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 56 regarding the income tax exemption of Professor Toshinosuke Muto.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Note No. 56 of March 4, 1941, regarding the tax exemption of Professor Toshinosuke Muto. The note confirms that a copy has been transmitted to the competent U.S. authority with a view to granting Muto an exemption from federal income tax on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Acknowledging Note No. 56 Regarding Toshinosuke Muto

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that income tax exemption instructions will be issued for Rokuro Nagao of the Imperial Japanese Army Inspector's Office.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan replies to State's letter of March 3, 1941, regarding Rokuro Nagao, Assistant Military Engineer at the Imperial Japanese Army Inspector's Office in New York City. The letter notes State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. Sullivan confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Rokuro Nagao

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy notifies the Secretary of State of the departure of Tateki Nakamura and requests assistance with his sailing permit.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy informs the Department of State that Tateki Nakamura, Secretary to the Financial Department attached to the Japanese Financial Commission in New York, will depart from Los Angeles on March 24, 1941, on the Tatuta Maru. The Embassy requests that his income tax exemption be confirmed so he may obtain his sailing permit in New York prior to leaving. Pages 8 and 9 are duplicate copies of the note.
subfiles.title: Note No. 66 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Concerning the Departure of Tateki Nakamura

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that arrangements have been requested for Tateki Nakamura's sailing document in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 66 of March 12, 1941, concerning Tateki Nakamura's scheduled departure on the Tatuta Maru. The note states that the request was communicated by telephone to the competent authorities to effectuate his income tax exemption. It confirms that arrangements were requested for Nakamura to receive his sailing document in New York City prior to departure.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding the Departure of Tateki Nakamura

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles certifies Section 116(h) tax exemption for Tateki Nakamura of the Japanese Financial Commission.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles confirms a March 18 telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Tateki Nakamura of the Japanese Financial Commission. Welles certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, affirming that Japan grants an equivalent exemption to U.S. employees. The letter notes Nakamura's planned departure from Los Angeles on the Tatuta Maru and his request for a sailing document in New York.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Tateki Nakamura
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that tax exemption instructions will be issued for Assistant Professor Goro Fukuyama.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of March 7 concerning Goro Fukuyama, Assistant Professor of Hokkaido Imperial University sent to study forest technology. The Treasury notes the State Department's reciprocity certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. Sullivan confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Goro Fukuyama

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Takehiko Uyeda of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan replies to State's letter of March 4 confirming a February 21 phone message regarding Takehiko Uyeda of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York. Uyeda scheduled departure from San Francisco on March 13, 1941, and desired a sailing document before leaving New York. In view of State's Section 116(h) certification, appropriate instructions are being issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Takehiko Uyeda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that tax exemption instructions will be issued for Dr. Kentaro Shimizu of Tokyo Imperial University.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan responds to State's letter of March 7 concerning Dr. Kentaro Shimizu, an Assistant at Tokyo Imperial University sent to the United States to study neurological surgery. The Treasury takes note of State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. Sullivan states that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Kentaro Shimizu

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for seven officials attached to the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy requests that seven Japanese officials attached to the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office at 1 Madison Avenue, New York City, be granted exemption from income taxes. The attached list names Engineer Captain Yuzo Isikawa, Engineer Commander Masao Sasaki, Paymaster Commander Sadaki Osuga, Commander Iwao Arisaka, and Assistant Engineers Kuniji Ozawa, Masao Nakamoto, and Minoru Shirai, specifying their arrival dates and vessels. Page 18 is a duplicate of the note.
subfiles.title: Note No. 68 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Requesting Tax Exemption for Naval Inspector's Office Personnel

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles certifies Section 116(h) tax exemption for seven officials of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office.
subfiles.summary: Sumner Welles transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 68 to the Secretary of the Treasury. He certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. personnel and that the services performed by the seven Japanese naval officers and engineers in New York are similar in character to those of U.S. employees abroad.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Naval Inspector's Office Personnel

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Note No. 68 regarding tax exemption for personnel of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 68 of March 12, 1941, regarding officials attached to the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York. The note confirms that a copy of the request has been transmitted to the competent U.S. authority to effectuate their income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Acknowledging Note No. 68 Regarding Naval Inspector's Office Personnel

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Kiyoshi Murai of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan replies to State's letter of March 10 confirming a February 27 phone call regarding Kiyoshi Murai of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York. Murai scheduled departure from New York on March 5 aboard the Asozan Maru. Based on State's Section 116(h) reciprocity certification, Sullivan confirms that instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Kiyoshi Murai

subfiles.about: Kango Iguchi of Toa Kigyo Corporation requests State Department certification of his resident alien status to secure an income tax sailing permit.
subfiles.summary: Kango Iguchi of Toa Kigyo Corporation in New York writes to the Department of State requesting certification that he is a resident alien for income tax and sailing permit purposes. Having resided in the U.S. since 1935 as a treaty merchant, he has been transferred back to Japan and plans to leave New York around March 22, 1941. He provides his vessel of arrival, passport classification, and Alien Registration Number.
subfiles.title: Letter from Kango Iguchi to the Department of State Requesting Alien Resident Certification for Sailing Permit

subfiles.about: The Department of State informs Kango Iguchi that sailing permits are outside its jurisdiction and refers his request to the Bureau of Internal Revenue.
subfiles.from: Nathaniel P. Davis (Chief, Division of Foreign Service Administration, for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Nathaniel P. Davis, Chief of the Division of Foreign Service Administration, acknowledges receipt of Kango Iguchi's letter of March 15 regarding his desire to obtain a sailing document. Davis informs Iguchi that the matter is not within the jurisdiction of the Department of State. A copy of Iguchi's letter has been referred to the Bureau of Internal Revenue in Washington for attention.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Department of State to Kango Iguchi Referring Sailing Permit Inquiry to Bureau of Internal Revenue

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State of the scheduled departure of Professor Kenzo Nagai and requests a sailing permit.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy informs the Department of State that Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University, sent to study electrical engineering and communication, will depart from San Francisco on April 17, 1941, on the Kamakura Maru. The Embassy requests that authorities be notified of his tax-exempt status so he may obtain a sailing permit in San Francisco. Page 27 is a duplicate copy of the note.
subfiles.title: Note No. 77 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Concerning the Departure of Kenzo Nagai

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State notifies the Japanese Ambassador that arrangements have been requested for Kenzo Nagai's sailing document in San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Note No. 77 of March 18, 1941, regarding Professor Kenzo Nagai's departure on the Kamakura Maru. The note states that the request was communicated by telephone to the competent authorities to effectuate Nagai's tax exemption. It confirms that arrangements have been requested for him to receive his sailing document upon arrival in San Francisco.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding the Departure of Kenzo Nagai

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles certifies Section 116(h) tax exemption for Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University.
subfiles.summary: Sumner Welles confirms a March 19 telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University. Welles formally certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, stating that Japan grants an equivalent exemption to U.S. Government employees. The letter notes Nagai's planned departure from San Francisco on the Kamakura Maru and his request to obtain his sailing document there.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Kenzo Nagai
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges certification and confirms tax exemption instructions for Professor Toshinosuke Muto.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan replies to State's letter of March 15 concerning Professor Toshinosuke Muto of Kyushu Imperial University, sent to the United States for atomic research. Sullivan acknowledges State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. He confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Toshinosuke Muto

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for three officials attached to the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy requests that three officials attached to the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau at 261 Fifth Avenue, New York City, be granted exemption from income taxes. The attached list names Shiro Suzuki (Government Silk Conditioning House), Yukio Suetugu (Department of Agriculture and Forestry), and Syokiti Mogami (Department of Agriculture and Forestry), who arrived in San Francisco on February 20, 1941, aboard the Yawata Maru.
subfiles.title: Note No. 80 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Requesting Tax Exemption for Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau Personnel

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State requests Foreign Official Status Notification forms for three officials of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese Note No. 80 of March 24 regarding Shiro Suzuki, Yukio Suetugu, and Syokiti Mogami of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau. In accordance with the Department's circular note of December 16, 1940, the Embassy is requested to have these officials complete and submit Foreign Official Status Notification forms to regularize their status.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Requesting Status Forms for Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau Personnel

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State requests Foreign Official Status Notification forms under the Alien Registration Act for seven naval inspectorate officers.
subfiles.summary: Referring to Japanese Note No. 68 of March 12, the Secretary of State explains that foreign government officials must notify the Department to claim exemption under the Alien Registration Act of 1940 and regularize their status. The Ambassador is requested to have the seven listed officials attached to the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office complete and submit Foreign Official Status Notification forms in duplicate. Page 38 provides the list of seven officers: Yuzo Isikawa, Masao Sasaki, Sadaki Osuga, Iwao Arisaka, Kuniji Ozawa, Masao Nakamoto, and Minoru Shirai.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Requesting Status Forms for Naval Inspector's Office Personnel

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles certifies Section 116(h) tax exemption for three Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau officials.
subfiles.summary: Sumner Welles transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 80 to the Secretary of the Treasury regarding Shiro Suzuki, Yukio Suetugu, and Syokiti Mogami of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York. Welles certifies that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. Government employees and that their duties are similar in character to those performed by U.S. employees abroad.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau Personnel
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 80 regarding tax exemption for personnel of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 80 of March 24, 1941, concerning officials at the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau. The note confirms that a copy has been sent to the competent U.S. authority to effectuate exemption from federal income tax on their official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Acknowledging Note No. 80 Regarding Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau Personnel

subfiles.about: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires notifies the State Department of Tadao Furuta's travel schedule and requests sailing permits.
subfiles.from: Japanese Embassy, Washington (Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim)
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim informs the Secretary of State of the departure plans of Tadao Furuta, Secretary to the Financial Commissioner in New York. Furuta plans to leave Miami on February 25 to visit Cuba, return on February 27 to visit Panama and Mexico, and sail from Los Angeles for Japan on March 10 on the Asama Maru. The Embassy requests that authorities be notified so Furuta can obtain sailing permits at Miami and Los Angeles. Page 43 is a duplicate copy.
subfiles.title: Note No. 29 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Concerning the Departure of Tadao Furuta

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 29 and confirms telephone notification regarding Tadao Furuta's tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 29 of February 5, 1941, regarding Tadao Furuta's travel through Cuba, Panama, Mexico, and Los Angeles. The note confirms that the information was immediately communicated by telephone to the competent authorities to facilitate Furuta's income tax exemption on official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Regarding Tadao Furuta

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Tadao Furuta.
subfiles.summary: Cordell Hull confirms a February 7 telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Tadao Furuta, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commissioner in New York. Hull details Furuta's itinerary through Miami, Cuba, Panama, Mexico, and Los Angeles aboard the Asama Maru. Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Tadao Furuta
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Tateki Nakamura of the Japanese Financial Commission.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan responds to State's letter of March 21 confirming a March 13 phone call regarding Tateki Nakamura of the Japanese Financial Commission. Sullivan notes Nakamura's planned departure on the Tatuta Maru from Los Angeles and his request for a sailing document in New York. Based on State's Section 116(h) certification, instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Tateki Nakamura

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for personnel of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges State's letter of March 22 enclosing the list of officials at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York. The letter takes note of State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. Sullivan confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Naval Inspector's Office Personnel

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Professor Kenzo Nagai.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan responds to State's letter of March 27 confirming a phone message of March 19 regarding Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University. Nagai scheduled departure from San Francisco on April 17 on the Kamakura Maru and wished to receive his sailing document there. In view of State's Section 116(h) certification, instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Kenzo Nagai

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for officials of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges State's letter of March 29 enclosing the Japanese Embassy's note regarding personnel at the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York. The Treasury notes State's reciprocity certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. Sullivan confirms that instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau Personnel

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet records a report from Vancouver concerning Tadao Wikawa preparing for the visit of Colonel Iwakuro.
subfiles.summary: This State Department cross-reference file note indexes a despatch dated February 25, 1941, from Consul Smith at Vancouver (originally filed under 711.94/1973). The referenced paper reports on the visit of Tadao Wikawa to the United States to prepare for the arrival of Colonel Iwakuro, described as one of the driving forces of the Japanese Army. The cross-reference was filed under decimal file 894.01B11/318.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Visit of Tadao Wikawa and Colonel Iwakuro

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy informs the Secretary of State of Takeo Kimura's departure and requests a sailing permit in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy notifies the Department of State of the impending departure of Takeo Kimura, Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of the Department of Naval Aeronautics attached to the Navy Inspector's Office in New York. Kimura plans to sail from Seattle on May 9, 1941, aboard the Hikawa Maru. The Embassy requests that authorities be informed so he may obtain his sailing permit in New York before traveling to Seattle.
subfiles.title: Note No. 110 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Concerning the Departure of Takeo Kimura

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 110 and confirms notification of authorities regarding Takeo Kimura's sailing permit.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 110 of April 22, 1941, regarding Takeo Kimura's departure on the Hikawa Maru from Seattle. The note states that the matter has been transmitted to the competent authority to effectuate Kimura's tax exemption. Attention was specifically drawn to Kimura's request to obtain his sailing permit before leaving New York.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding the Departure of Takeo Kimura

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies Section 116(h) tax exemption for Takeo Kimura of the Japanese Navy Inspector's Office.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 110 to the Secretary of the Treasury regarding Takeo Kimura. Hull notes Kimura's scheduled sailing from Seattle on the Hikawa Maru and his desire to obtain a sailing permit in New York. Formal reciprocity certification is provided under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Takeo Kimura
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Takeo Kimura.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of April 29 regarding Takeo Kimura of the Japanese Department of Naval Aeronautics. Sullivan notes Kimura's planned departure from Seattle on May 9 and his request for a sailing permit in New York. In view of State's certification under Section 116(h), instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Takeo Kimura

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests the refund of a $35.79 customs bond deposited by railway engineer Jiro Tachibana upon his urgent departure for Germany.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy refers to earlier correspondence regarding Jiro Tachibana, Engineer of the Department of Japanese Government Railways. Ordered urgently to Germany, Tachibana secured a last-minute cancellation ticket on the Yankee Clipper from New York on April 23, 1941, leaving no time to notify authorities in advance. Prior to departing, he was required to deposit a $35.79 bond with the Collector of Customs at New York. The Ambassador requests that this bond payment be refunded to the Embassy for transmission to Tachibana.
subfiles.title: Note No. 119 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Requesting Refund of Customs Bond for Jiro Tachibana

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Note No. 119 and states that the bond refund request has been referred to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 119 of May 7, 1941, requesting the refund of a $35.79 bond deposited by Jiro Tachibana with the Collector of Customs at New York. The note states that a copy has been transmitted to the Treasury Department. The Secretary of State promises to communicate further with the Ambassador upon receiving Treasury's reply.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Customs Bond Refund for Jiro Tachibana

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits the Japanese Embassy's request for a refund of Jiro Tachibana's customs bond to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to earlier correspondence certifying tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Jiro Tachibana of the Japanese Government Railways. A copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 119 is enclosed, explaining Tachibana's departure on the Yankee Clipper and the deposit of a $35.79 bond with the Collector of Customs at New York. The Secretary requests Treasury's advice on the proper reply to be made to the Ambassador.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Customs Bond Refund for Jiro Tachibana

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy notifies the State Department of Professor Toshinosuke Muto's departure schedule and requests a sailing permit in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy informs the Department of State that Professor Toshinosuke Muto of Kyushu Imperial University plans to depart San Francisco on July 3, 1941, on the Kamakura Maru. Muto expects to leave New York around May 25 and wishes to obtain his sailing permit at the Customs Office in New York before that date. The Embassy requests that appropriate authorities be notified to facilitate the permit.
subfiles.title: Note No. 120 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Concerning the Departure of Toshinosuke Muto

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that Internal Revenue has been requested to issue Muto's sailing document in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 120 of May 9 regarding Professor Toshinosuke Muto. The note confirms that the information was communicated by telephone to the Bureau of Internal Revenue. It was requested that a sailing document be issued to Muto in New York before May 25, prior to his departure for San Francisco.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding the Departure of Toshinosuke Muto

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies Section 116(h) tax exemption for Professor Toshinosuke Muto in connection with his departure.
subfiles.summary: Cordell Hull confirms a May 14 telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Professor Toshinosuke Muto of Kyushu Imperial University, residing at 640 Riverside Drive, New York City. The letter notes Muto's scheduled departure from San Francisco on July 3 and his request for a sailing document in New York before May 25. Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.

subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Department of State requests that Japanese official Minoru Takada complete a Foreign Official Status Notification form.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State informs the Japanese Embassy that it was notified of the arrival of Minoru Takada at San Francisco on March 21, 1940, to reside in the United States as an official or employee of the Japanese Government. In conformity with circular note of December 16, 1940, the Embassy is requested to have Takada complete and return the enclosed Foreign Official Status Notification form in duplicate.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Department of State to the Japanese Embassy Regarding Minoru Takada

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy replies that Minoru Takada already departed the United States in February 1941.
subfiles.summary: Replying to the State Department's memorandum of April 4, 1941, the Japanese Embassy states that Mr. Minoru Takada notified the Embassy by letter that he had already left the United States on February 24, 1941, departing from New Orleans via San Francisco.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Japanese Embassy to the Department of State Concerning the Departure of Minoru Takada

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Colonel Kenkiti Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Nobuo Masuda.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy requests that two Japanese army officers attached to the Imperial Japanese Army Inspector's Office at 1775 Broadway, New York City, be granted income tax exemption. The attached list specifies Colonel Kenkiti Sinjo, Japanese Army Language Officer, and Lieutenant Colonel Nobuo Masuda, Japanese Army Ordnance Inspector, both of whom arrived in San Francisco on March 20, 1941, aboard the Tatuta Maru.
subfiles.title: Note No. 122 from the Japanese Embassy to the Secretary of State Requesting Tax Exemption for Army Inspector's Office Personnel

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies Section 116(h) tax exemption for Colonel Kenkiti Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Nobuo Masuda.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 122 regarding Colonel Kenkiti Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Nobuo Masuda of the Imperial Japanese Army Inspector's Office in New York. Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. personnel and that their official services are similar in character to those of U.S. officers abroad.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Colonel Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Masuda
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 122 concerning tax exemption for Colonel Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Masuda.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 122 of May 12, 1941, regarding Colonel Kenkiti Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Nobuo Masuda of the Imperial Japanese Army Inspector's Office in New York. The note confirms that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority with a view to granting exemption from federal income tax on their official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Acknowledging Note No. 122 Regarding Colonel Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Masuda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Toshinosuke Muto in connection with his departure.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan responds to State's letter of May 16 confirming a May 14 phone message regarding Professor Toshinosuke Muto. Sullivan notes Muto's planned sailing from San Francisco on July 3 and his request for a sailing document in New York before May 25. Based on State's Section 116(h) certification, appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Toshinosuke Muto

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department informs the State Department that Jiro Tachibana's customs bond refund request is under consideration.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges State's letter of May 19 regarding Jiro Tachibana of the Japanese Government Railways. The letter references Tachibana's departure on the Yankee Clipper and the $35.79 bond deposited with the Collector of Customs at New York. Sullivan states that the refund matter will be given careful consideration and a further reply will follow as soon as possible.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Customs Bond Refund for Jiro Tachibana

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Colonel Kenkiti Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Nobuo Masuda.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of May 23 enclosing Japanese Note No. 122. The letter concerns the income tax exemption of Colonel Kenkiti Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Nobuo Masuda of the Imperial Japanese Army Inspector's Office in New York. Taking note of State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Sullivan confirms that instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Colonel Sinjo and Lieutenant Colonel Masuda

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy notifies the Department of State of the transfer, renaming, and staff title changes of the Raw Silk Bureau in New York.
keywords: Raw Silk Bureau of New York
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy informs the Department of State that the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau of New York was transferred on April 1, 1941, from the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry to the Bureau of Trade of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The office is renamed The Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau of New York. The note details updated titles for staff members Syokiti Mogami (Director), Yukio Suetugu (Technical Expert), and Motonaga Ohto (Attaché).
subfiles.title: Note No. 151 from the Japanese Embassy to the Department of State Concerning Reorganization of the Raw Silk Bureau of New York
